## Executive Summary
Nikunj Garg is a results-driven Java Backend Developer engineering scalable backend architectures, high-concurrency systems, and real-time distributed services with Java 21, Spring Boot 3, PostgreSQL, and Redis. He specializes in eliminating data race conditions and inventory overselling via JPA/Hibernate pessimistic row locking, Redisson distributed MultiLocks, and ACID transactions, architecting low-latency REST APIs, and deploying bidirectional WebSockets (STOMP) with stateless JWT authentication pipelines. BCA student at Shri Guru Ram Rai University (SGRRU, Dehradun), and builder of production-grade systems including DevTinder, LibroSphere, and TicketWave.

## Major Projects

### 1. DevTinder — Developer Teammate Matching Platform (Backend Flagship)
- **Overview**: Teammate matchmaking platform originally prototyped during Devlynix Buildathon 2.0 with frontend teammates, then independently evolved and elevated into a production-grade backend service powering a Next.js client.
- **Tech Stack**: Java 21, Spring Boot 3, PostgreSQL, WebSockets (STOMP), Spring Security 6 (JWT & Refresh Token Rotation), Docker, Render Cloud.
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/gargnikunj991-ux/Devlynix-Buildathon-2.0.git
- **Key Capabilities**: Bidirectional STOMP WebSocket broker with delta query synchronization (`?after={id}`) and unread tracking over normalized schemas; candidate discovery service ranking profiles dynamically by shared skill counts and mutual swipe constraints; stateless Spring Security filters with Refresh Token Rotation, sliding-window IP rate limiting (`RateLimitFilter`), incoming match radar, and queue rewind; multi-stage Docker containerization with `/api/health` monitoring for cloud deployment.

### 2. LibroSphere — High-Concurrency Asset Lending & Reservation Engine
- **Overview**: High-concurrency asset lending and reservation backend engineered to eliminate race conditions, duplicate allocations, and inventory underflow under peak multi-threaded contention.
- **Tech Stack**: Java 21, Spring Boot 3, PostgreSQL, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate ORM, JUnit 5.
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/gargnikunj991-ux/library_spring.git
- **Key Capabilities**: Database row-level pessimistic write locking (`@Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)` / `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) inside atomic `@Transactional` boundaries completely preventing double-checkout TOCTOU anomalies; automated FIFO reservation waitlist queue (`WAITING` -> `NOTIFIED_READY`) with 48-hour pickup reservations; nightly overdue fine reconciliation cron worker (`@Scheduled`) with composite B-Tree indexes on `(returned, due_date)` to avoid full table scans; automated JUnit 5 integration test suite simulating concurrent checkout worker threads (`CountDownLatch`) validating 100% thread safety, expected rejections, and zero underflow.

### 3. TicketWave — Ultra-Scale Distributed Seat Hold & Checkout Engine
- **Overview**: High-throughput distributed event ticketing engine engineered to handle massive flash-crowd concurrency spikes with zero seat overselling, distributed deadlock elimination, and financial idempotency.
- **Tech Stack**: Java 21, Spring Boot 3.3.4, Redis 7, Redisson MultiLock, PostgreSQL, Spring Data JPA, Micrometer, JUnit 5.
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/gargnikunj991-ux/TicketWave.git
- **Key Capabilities**: Distributed seat hold allocation using Redisson MultiLock (<1ms) with deterministic natural seat-ID sorting to eliminate distributed deadlocks under peak arena traffic; in-memory Redis SETNX idempotency gate (`IN_PROGRESS` 120s / `COMPLETED` 24h replay) with decoupled payment execution outside DB boundaries preventing HikariCP pool exhaustion; dual-tier inventory reclamation combining reactive Redis keyspace expiration pub/sub (`__keyevent@*__:expired`) with a 60-second scheduled PostgreSQL sweeper; comprehensive 70-test JUnit 5 suite featuring 100-thread single-seat contention stress tests, duplicate checkout idempotency storms, and architectural failure-mode simulations verifying ACID resilience.
